statement: For an n x n square matrix A, the characteristic polynomial is the monic polynomial of degree n defined by p_A(t) = det(tI - A), whose roots are precisely the eigenvalues of A.

symbols.meaning: Square matrix representing a linear transformation
Non-zero eigenvector corresponding to eigenvalue λ
Eigenvalue scalar corresponding to eigenvector v
Dimension of the square matrix A

steps.text: For a linear transformation represented by a square matrix A, an eigenvector v and the corresponding eigenvalue λ satisfy the equation A v = λ v, with v ≠ 0.
Rewriting λ v as λ I v, the eigenvalue equation is equivalently expressed as (λ I - A) v = 0.
Because the eigenvector must be non-zero (v ≠ 0), the matrix (λ I - A) must be singular, which requires its determinant to vanish: det(λ I - A) = 0.

Replacing the scalar λ with an indeterminate variable t (or x), the eigenvalues of A are the roots of det(tI - A) = 0, which defines the characteristic polynomial p_A(t) = det(tI - A), a monic polynomial in t of degree n.

assumptions.assumption: A is a square matrix (n x n)
assumptions.breaks_when: A is rectangular (m x n with m ≠ n), making tI - A undefined and preventing determinant computation
v = 0, which trivially satisfies (λI - A)v = 0 for every λ and fails to force singularity of (λI - A)

assumptions.assumption: The scalar field is algebraically closed when full factorization into linear factors is required
assumptions.breaks_when: The matrix entries belong to a field that is not algebraically closed (such as the real numbers) and roots of p_A(t) lie in an extension field

failure_modes.signature: Matrix dimension mismatch in tI - A; determinant cannot be evaluated
failure_modes.cause: A has non-equal row and column dimensions (m ≠ n)

failure_modes.signature: Every scalar λ appears as a solution to A v = λ v
failure_modes.cause: v = 0 satisfies the linear equation for any λ without requiring det(λI - A) = 0

failure_modes.mode: Absence of eigenvalues in the base field
failure_modes.signature: p_A(t) has no roots or incomplete linear factorization over the base field
failure_modes.cause: The base field is not algebraically closed (e.g., real matrices with complex conjugate eigenvalues)

instantiation.why_here: Nothing in agrios_ws computes a characteristic polynomial. robot_localization's own source is not shown, so there is no evidence that the library computes one either. The concept shows up because the components set square matrices: the 15x15 process_noise_covariance and initial_estimate_covariance in both EKFs, and the 6x6 twist covariance that odom_cov_relay sends. Every one of these is diagonal. For a diagonal matrix, det(tI - A) is the product of (t - a_ii), so you can read the eigenvalues straight off the diagonal without expanding a determinant.

concrete.in_your_project: Any of the square matrices the project sets. Examples: process_noise_covariance (15x15, diagonal) in ekf_global.yaml and ekf_local.yaml, initial_estimate_covariance (15x15, diagonal), or the 6x6 twist covariance built in odom_cov_relay.py lines 12-16.
15 for process_noise_covariance and initial_estimate_covariance. 6 for the twist covariance that odom_cov_relay.py fills as a 36-entry list.
The 15x15 identity for the EKF covariance parameters, or the 6x6 identity for the odom_cov_relay twist covariance.

For process_noise_covariance it is (t-0.05)^2 (t-0.06)^2 (t-0.03)^2 (t-0.025)^2 (t-0.04)(t-0.01)^4 (t-0.02)(t-0.015)^2, from diagonal entries 0-14. That is monic and of degree 15. For initial_estimate_covariance it is (t - 1e-9)^15.

The diagonal entries, with repeated roots counted once per entry. For process_noise_covariance: 0.05 (entries 0, 1), 0.06 (2, 5), 0.03 (3, 4), 0.025 (6, 7), 0.04 (8), 0.01 (9, 10, 12, 13), 0.02 (11), 0.015 (14). For initial_estimate_covariance: 1e-9, repeated 15 times. For the odom_cov_relay twist covariance: 0.05 (c[0], vx), 0.05 (c[7], vy), 0.02 (c[35], vyaw), plus three zero eigenvalues from the diagonal slots left at 0.0. This assumes the 36-entry list is 6x6 row-major, so that indices 0, 7 and 35 are diagonal.
For any of these diagonal matrices, the standard basis vector e_i (15x1 or 6x1) is an eigenvector for the eigenvalue at diagonal position i.

knobs.means: Sets a diagonal 15x15 matrix, so its characteristic polynomial splits into 15 linear factors (t - d_i). Each diagonal value d_i is an eigenvalue. Values that repeat (such as 0.01 at entries 9, 10, 12 and 13) are repeated roots.
Has the same diagonal values as in ekf_global.yaml, so it has the same characteristic polynomial and the same eigenvalues.
Sets a diagonal 15x15 matrix with every entry equal to 1e-9. Its characteristic polynomial is (t - 1e-9)^15: one eigenvalue of multiplicity 15.
Is identical to the ekf_global.yaml value: p_A(t) = (t - 1e-9)^15.

instantiation.notation: The sheet uses A for a generic square matrix. Here the matrices it applies to are named process_noise_covariance and initial_estimate_covariance in the config, and msg.twist.covariance in odom_cov_relay.py.
